record.paper_title: A UNIFIED ANALYSIS OF LINEAR QUATERNION DYNAMIC EQUATIONS ON TIME SCALES
record.context_brief: Putzer parameter selection for quaternion matrices
record.original_question: What theory and algorithms can resolve the selection problem for the constants alpha_1,...,alpha_m in Putzer's algorithm for homogeneous linear quaternion dynamic equations on time scales: given a constant quaternion matrix A in H^{n x n}, choose quaternion constants alpha_i so that P_0=I_n and P_k=A P_{k-1}-P_{k-1} alpha_k eventually satisfy P_m=0, making the Putzer fundamental-solution construction usable, including for matrices without enough right linearly independent eigenvectors?

evidence.quote: Although there are some theoretical challenges on selections of α1, α2, · · ·, αm, the Putzer’s algorithm is still feasible.

artifact.category_tag: Quaternion dynamic equations on time scales
artifact.status_search_result: The Putzer-type construction for linear quaternion dynamic equations on time scales is acknowledged in the available literature as having "theoretical challenges" regarding the selection of the quaternion constants $\alpha_i$, with no general theory or algorithm characterizing admissible selections having been located. Standard Putzer references treat only the commutative (real/complex) case via eigenvalue ordering, which does not extend directly to the non-commutative quaternion setting. No subsequent work resolving the selection problem in full generality was found.

status_evidence.title: A unified analysis of linear quaternion dynamic equations on time scales
status_evidence.snippet: Although there are some theoretical challenges on selections of α1, α2, ···, αm, the Putzer's algorithm is still feasible.
status_evidence.claim: The selection of the quaternion constants in Putzer's algorithm is explicitly described as a theoretical challenge, indicating the problem is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Putzer's Algorithm (Lebovitz notes)
status_evidence.snippet: Putzer's algorithm computes e^{At} using eigenvalues of A arranged in a specific order.
status_evidence.claim: Classical Putzer theory relies on commutative scalar eigenvalues, which does not directly extend to quaternions.
